# WESSAAL Linked Devices API v1 — full reference

Canonical documentation: https://docs.wessaal.com/
Quickstart: https://docs.wessaal.com/quickstart/
Authentication: https://docs.wessaal.com/authentication/
Endpoints: https://docs.wessaal.com/endpoints/
Webhooks/status: https://docs.wessaal.com/webhooks/

## API origin
Production base path: https://app.wessaal.com/integration/v1
Use HTTPS and JSON request bodies.

## Authentication
Send X-API-Key: YOUR_API_KEY on each request. This is not HTTP Bearer auth. Scope each key to the minimum permissions: send_message, read_messages, manage_instances, manage_contacts, manage_templates and manage_workspaces. Store the key server-side and rotate any exposed key.

## First requests
1. GET /ping confirms valid API key (pong on success).
2. GET /me inspects the key owner and permissions.
3. GET /instances selects a sender (manage_instances permission).
4. POST /messages/send queues a message (send_message permission).
5. GET /messages/{messageId}/status polls the resulting message (read_messages permission).

## Core endpoints
GET /ping
GET /me
GET /instances
GET /instances/{instanceId}
GET /instances/{instanceId}/status
POST /messages/send
POST /messages/send-bulk
POST /messages/send-group
GET /messages
GET /messages/{messageId}
GET /messages/{messageId}/status
GET /groups
POST /instances/{instanceId}/sync-address-book
GET /contacts
POST /contacts
GET /contacts/{contactId}
PUT /contacts/{contactId}
DELETE /contacts/{contactId}
GET /templates
POST /templates

## WhatsApp group messages
Import and synchronize groups from a connected instance first. GET /groups returns local numeric IDs. For POST /messages/send-group, provide instance, group_id, content and a unique Idempotency-Key request header. HTTP 202 only indicates queue acceptance. Some group-send features are environment-gated. Staging dry_run validation is not real delivery.

## Response codes
200: Successful reads or supported reused/bulk operations.
201: Created resource.
202: Accepted for asynchronous queueing — not delivery.
402: Insufficient credits.
403: Permission, workspace or outbound-policy restriction.
404: Resource not found or unavailable to the key owner.
409: State/idempotency conflict where applicable.
422: Invalid request or unsupported operation.
500: Unexpected server error.

## Webhooks and event integrity
The currently published Linked Devices integration API reference does not define a customer-configurable webhook subscription route, canonical event types or a signature-verification protocol. Do not invent a webhook endpoint or claim event delivery. Use GET /messages/{messageId}/status and server-side backoff polling until an authoritative webhook contract is published.

The public docs describe an integration contract, not proof that every optional capability is enabled in a particular account.
